patient.chief_complaint: Confusion and agitation after brief seizure, not returning to normal after 40 minutes, fever noted by EMS
patient.hpi: A 34-year-old White female graphic designer was brought by EMS to the emergency department after her roommate found her having a brief generalized seizure lasting 2 minutes and called 911. The roommate reports the patient had been unwell for 5 days with progressively worsening headache, confusion, and behavioral changes — she was talking to herself, becoming paranoid, and at one point undressing in the living room. She had reduced oral intake for 3 days. The roommate noted the patient had no history of seizures. On EMS arrival, the patient was minimally responsive, combative, with a temperature of 38.9°C measured by EMS. In the ED she is markedly agitated, requiring soft restraints, not following commands, with disorganized speech, and responding to internal stimuli (appears to be hallucinating). Her roommate does not know of any recent illness, travel, tick bites, or animal exposures. The patient is otherwise healthy with no known medical conditions. She was previously a college athlete. Social history: non-smoker, rare social alcohol, no illicit drugs per roommate (though roommate acknowledges she may not know everything). Single, lives with roommate, no family in the area. Parents are being contacted. The roommate found an almost-empty bottle of ibuprofen in the bathroom but states the patient usually takes it for headaches. There are no other medications visible in the apartment. The patient wore a medic alert bracelet that says 'no known allergies.'

eeg.impression: ABNORMAL EEG. Non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) with right temporal predominance on diffuse encephalitic background. Clinical correlation recommended.

ct.impression: Normal non-contrast CT head. No hemorrhage, no mass. Normal CT does not exclude encephalitis. MRI brain with gadolinium required. Consider pelvic ultrasound or CT pelvis in young woman with suspected anti-NMDAR encephalitis to evaluate for ovarian teratoma.

LP for CSF analysis and autoimmune antibody panel
Empiric acyclovir 10 mg/kg q8h IV immediately

output.impression: Limbic encephalitis pattern: bilateral mesial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity involving hippocampi and amygdalae, with basal ganglia involvement. No DWI restriction. Leptomeningeal enhancement. Ovarian teratoma must be urgently excluded. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description: 6.8 x 5.2 cm right ovarian cystic mass with mixed solid and cystic components, fat-containing elements (T1 bright, T2 heterogeneous) — mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst)

output.impression: Right ovarian mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst), 6.8 cm. This is the paraneoplastic trigger for anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Laparoscopic right salpingo-oophorectomy is urgently indicated — tumor removal is the definitive treatment and markedly improves neurological recovery.
recommended_actions: Urgent gynecology consultation for laparoscopic right salpingo-oophorectomy
Tumor removal is the most effective treatment and should not be delayed

output.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis treatment immunotherapy teratoma outcome

results.title: Treatment and prognostic factors for long-term outcome in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis
results.key_finding: 80% of patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis recover fully or near-fully with immunotherapy. Tumor removal (in those with teratoma) + first-line immunotherapy (steroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis) is standard. Second-line agents (rituximab, cyclophosphamide) for refractory cases. Recovery may take weeks to months.

output.summary: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis: first-line treatment = IV methylprednisolone + IVIG ± plasmapheresis. Ovarian teratoma removal is mandatory when found — dramatically improves outcomes. 80% full/near-full recovery expected. NCSE in anti-NMDAR responds to immunotherapy rather than AED escalation alone.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE), associated with right ovarian teratoma

differential.key_features: CSF HSV PCR negative; MRI shows bilateral limbic/temporal signal (HSV typically unilateral temporal with hemorrhagic necrosis); no hemorrhagic changes on imaging
CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis (not neutrophilic); Gram stain and culture negative; procalcitonin mildly elevated but clinical picture more consistent with subacute encephalitis
Comprehensive urine drug screen negative; 5-day prodrome too long for acute ingestion; anti-NMDAR antibodies positive
Anti-NMDAR positive in both serum and CSF; other autoimmune antibodies negative; clinical phenotype (young woman + psychiatric prodrome + orofacial dyskinesias) is classic anti-NMDAR

optimal_actions.action: Emergent EEG for NCSE diagnosis and to identify extreme delta brush pattern
optimal_actions.expected_finding: NCSE with right temporal ictal activity; extreme delta brush (anti-NMDAR specific)

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage or mass
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal CT — autoimmune encephalitis often normal on CT

optimal_actions.action: Empiric acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h immediately — start before HSV PCR result (HSV encephalitis is fatal if not treated)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No adverse effects; can discontinue when HSV PCR negative

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain with gadolinium — evaluate for limbic encephalitis pattern
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral mesial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity — limbic encephalitis pattern

optimal_actions.action: LP for CSF: cell count, protein, glucose, HSV PCR, anti-NMDAR IgG antibody
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Lymphocytic pleocytosis; HSV PCR negative; anti-NMDAR IgG positive

optimal_actions.action: Initiate immunotherapy: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily x5 days after LP
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Gradual improvement in encephalopathy over days to weeks

optimal_actions.action: Pelvic imaging (MRI pelvis or CT abdomen/pelvis) to identify ovarian teratoma
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right ovarian teratoma 6.8 cm — paraneoplastic trigger

optimal_actions.action: Urgent gynecology consultation for laparoscopic right salpingo-oophorectomy — tumor removal is essential
Add IVIG 2 g/kg over 5 days in addition to steroids for combined first-line immunotherapy
Continuous cEEG monitoring 24-48 hours during acute illness and immunotherapy phase
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Extreme delta brush pattern; progressive NCSE resolution with immunotherapy

critical_actions: Empiric acyclovir IMMEDIATELY — before any test results; HSV encephalitis must not be missed
Anti-NMDAR IgG antibody in serum AND CSF — both needed for diagnosis
Pelvic imaging to find ovarian teratoma — tumor removal is the most effective treatment
IV methylprednisolone + IVIG after LP — immunotherapy is the primary treatment
LP before steroids — collect CSF before immunotherapy to preserve diagnostic yield
Continuous cEEG monitoring to track NCSE and identify extreme delta brush pattern
contraindicated_actions: Delaying LP and immunotherapy waiting for antibody results — empiric treatment must start based on clinical syndrome
Not performing pelvic imaging in young woman with anti-NMDAR encephalitis — 50% have teratoma, removal dramatically improves outcome
Relying solely on AED escalation without immunotherapy — NCSE in anti-NMDAR responds to immunotherapy, not just AEDs
Stopping acyclovir before HSV PCR result — fatal delay if HSV is present
key_reasoning_points: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis in young women: classic pentad of psychiatric prodrome → seizures → NCSE → movement disorders (orofacial dyskinesias) → autonomic instability
Extreme delta brush (EDB) on EEG is highly specific (>90%) for anti-NMDAR encephalitis — key EEG finding for diagnosis
50% of young women with anti-NMDAR encephalitis have ovarian teratoma — pelvic imaging is mandatory
Tumor removal (salpingo-oophorectomy) is the most effective treatment — accelerates recovery more than any immunotherapy alone
Anti-NMDAR IgG must be checked in BOTH serum and CSF — CSF positive in >95%, serum positive in ~85%
First-line immunotherapy: IV methylprednisolone + IVIG (and/or plasmapheresis); second-line: rituximab, cyclophosphamide for refractory cases

metadata.teaching_points: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis in young women; extreme delta brush on EEG; ovarian teratoma workup; immunotherapy primary treatment; CSF and serum antibodies
metadata.pitfalls: Missing pelvic teratoma; treating only with AEDs without immunotherapy; not starting empiric acyclovir pending HSV result
metadata.clinical_pearl: Young woman + psychiatric prodrome + orofacial dyskinesias + NCSE = anti-NMDAR encephalitis until proven otherwise. Get pelvic imaging. Extreme delta brush on EEG is diagnostic.
